comments.why: Implicit context solves context-passing across languages.
comments.text: Implicit context [1] was one of the coolest features of a programming language I’ve ever seen that no one has ever implemented. And I’m really not sure why. Not just Go but most languages have this context passing problem with varying degrees of solution quality, making this implicit and built in could have opened up so many possibilities, more than just arenas. comments.text: I remember first seeing this idea from Jai ( [VIDEO] ), and I'm happy it's landing in other languages. Zig went another direction and requires you to specify the allocator explicitly via a function parameter, which is understandable given the language's goal to make everything explicit.
